rationale: Evidence across cohorts of individuals with RNU2-2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE119) demonstrates that affected patients present with a constellation of clinical signs typical of severe DEEs—including severe to profound developmental delay/intellectual disability, refractory focal/generalized seizures, infantile spasms, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome-like electroclinical patterns, hyperkinetic movement disorders, respiratory dysrhythmias (hyperventilation/apnea), and hippocampal sclerosis. While certain papers term the presentation 'distinctive', the specific phenotypic findings individually and collectively overlap substantially with other coding and non-coding early-onset DEEs (such as RNU4-2-associated ReNU syndrome, Rett syndrome, Dravet syndrome, and STXBP1/CDKL5 encephalopathies). Consequently, clinical phenotyping alone cannot definitively isolate DEE119 without whole-genome or dedicated non-coding spliceosomal snRNA sequencing.

evidence.text: In a study of RNU2-2 pathogenic variants, patients exhibited severe to profound impairment, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus, hyperventilation, sleep apnea, sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges, and hippocampal sclerosis, which represent severe features that clinically overlap with other epileptic encephalopathies.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3). Electroencephalography showed sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges (n = 4) and hippocampal sclerosis on magnetic resonance imaging (n = 3).

evidence.text: Deep phenotyping of individuals with biallelic RNU2-2 variants revealed severe to profound intellectual disability, absence of ambulation and speech, hyperkinesia, and refractory seizures, predominantly infantile spasms and tonic seizures resembling a Lennox-Gastaut syndrome phenotype, presenting a phenotypic signature with significant overlap with complex pediatric epilepsies.

source.title: Phenotypic and transcriptomic characterization of biallelic RNU2‐2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: All individuals presented with a highly concordant, severe DEE, characterized by severe to profound intellectual disability, inability to walk or communicate, hyperkinesia, and refractory seizures. Infantile spasms and tonic seizures were the predominant seizure types and a Lennox-Gastaut syndrome-like phenotype was common. These individuals had a significantly similar phenotypic signature when compared with 703 individuals with complex pediatric epilepsies (two-sided Monte Carlo permutation test, p = .005).

evidence.text: Systematic analysis of 200 snRNA genes identified RNU2-2 variants across dominant and recessive cohorts presenting with frequent epilepsy and overlapping neurodevelopmental phenotypes comparable to ReNU syndrome (RNU4-2) and other dominant/recessive NDDs.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: Dominant and recessive RNU2-2 NDDs share overlapping clinical features, with frequent epilepsy... and establish RNU2-2 variants as a principal contributor to NDDs, nearly as prevalent as ReNU syndrome.

evidence.text: Screening of pediatric movement disorders identified de novo RNU2-2 variants in patients with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and hyperkinetic movement disorders, highlighting wide phenotypic variability from DEE to milder movement presentations that share features with other childhood hyperkinetic spliceosomopathies.

source.title: Prominent Movement Disorders in RNU2‐2‐Related Spliceosomopathy
source.journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
source.quote: We identified recurrent de novo RNU2-2 variants (n.35A > G and n.4G > A) in two patients with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and hyperkinetic movement disorders... Spliceosomopathies should be considered in neurodevelopmental disorders and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies with hyperkinetic features.

new_directions.question_text: Does the specific combination of early hyperkinesia/chorea, episodic central hyperventilation, and early hippocampal sclerosis provide a high positive predictive value for RNU2-2 variants when evaluated across large unsolved DEE registries?
new_directions.rationale: While individual features overlap with other DEEs (e.g., Rett syndrome hyperventilation, STXBP1 movement disorders), multivariate scoring of this feature triad could prioritize RNU2-2 targeted testing in low-resource settings.

new_directions.question_text: Can functional transcriptomic biomarkers, such as the U2-2 to U2-1 abundance ratio or tissue-specific alternate 3' splice site usage in fibroblasts, serve as conclusive non-genomic diagnostic assays for DEE119?
new_directions.rationale: Jackson et al. and Henry et al. identify U2-2:U2-1 ratio depletion and aberrant fibroblast splicing patterns, which could resolve variants of uncertain significance in non-coding snRNA genes.
